samples.summary: PPTX theme `<a:srgbClr val>` sink bypasses the new `toRgbHexColor` normalizer the diff establishes for every other color sink
samples.evidence: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:83-84` still does `const hex = escapeXmlAttr(toSrgbHex(theme.colors[role]))` → `<a:srgbClr val="${hex}"/>`, where `toSrgbHex` (theme.ts:64) is only `hex.replace(/^#/,'').toUpperCase()`. The diff's new invariant (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:52-60: "every attribute this function emits is either [0-9A-F]{6}, a closed ROLE_TO_SCHEME value, or a finite number") does not hold for this file because it never routes through `colorChildXml`. `themes[]` is stored verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot` and the new `assertValidSlidesBody` validates only that `themes` is an array (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:472-478), so an API caller can put `rgb(255,0,0)`, `''`, or `a"/><x y="` in `theme.colors[role]` and the exported deck carries a schema-invalid (escaped-but-non-hex) `ST_HexColorRGB` that PowerPoint refuses to open.

samples.summary: Sibling object-literal attribute lookups (`DASH_VAL`, `KIND_TO_OOXML`, `SIZE_TO_OOXML`, `BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE`) were left as prototype-chain-walking `Record` lookups after the diff converted ALGN/UNDERLINE/PRST/DOCX_ALIGNMENTS to Maps for exactly that reason
samples.evidence: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts:122/143 `DASH_VAL[stroke.dash] ?? 'dash'` → `<a:prstDash val="…"/>`; packages/slides/src/export/pptx/connector.ts:55-56 `KIND_TO_OOXML[a.kind] ?? 'triangle'` / `SIZE_TO_OOXML[a.size] ?? 'med'`; packages/slides/src/export/pptx/layout.ts:53 `BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE[layout.id] ?? 'blank'`. All four read persisted, PUT-settable values (`stroke.dash`, arrowhead kind/size, `layouts[].id` — none validated by the new `assertValidLayout`), so a stored `'constructor'`/`'toString'` resolves to an inherited `Object.prototype` member, survives the `??` fallback and is stringified into an OOXML attribute — the precise failure mode the diff documents at packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:62-69 and packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:110-118.

samples.summary: `PRST_BY_KIND` duplicates the `ShapeKind` union without an exhaustiveness check, so any kind missing from the new allowlist silently exports as `rect`
samples.evidence: `... as const satisfies readonly Exclude<ShapeKind,'freeform'>[]` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts:24-90) only proves each listed string IS a ShapeKind; it does not prove the list COVERS the union declared at packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:54-125. A kind added to the union later (or one accidentally omitted today) hits `PRST_BY_KIND.get(kind) ?? 'rect'` at shape.ts:96 and exports as a rectangle, breaking PPTX round-trip for that shape with no compile-time or test failure. A `Record<Exclude<ShapeKind,'freeform'>, string>` built into the Map, or a `satisfies` on an exhaustive record, would make omission a type error.

samples.summary: The newly documented "GET → edit → PUT stays lossless for docs bodies" contract is contradicted by the reader synthesizing blocks with an empty `id`, which the validator rejects with a 400
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:328-333 emits a placeholder block `{ id: '', type: 'paragraph', … }` for a table cell with no block children, and treeNodeToBlock uses `id: attrs.id ?? ''` (docs-tree.ts:369, 385). `assertValidBlock` requires a non-empty `id`, so PUTting back exactly what GET returned for such a document 400s. The id check predates this diff, but the losslessness claim added in rest-api.md:266-269 and the new cell/inline requirements make it a contract this change now asserts.

samples.summary: Inline-style clearing still uses the path-range `removeStyleByPath` the diff declares unsafe, while every other removal site was converted to the node-scoped `removeNodeStyle`
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1915 keeps `tree.removeStyleByPath([...blockPath, i], [...blockPath, i + 1], removeAttrs)`. The new helper's doc comment (same file, lines 258-272) states that a path range spans the node's whole subtree and that Yorkie applies the removal to every element node in it. It is (probably) harmless here because an inline node's children are text nodes, but it is the one remaining caller of the pattern the change declares wrong, and it will silently become wrong if inlines ever gain element children.

finding.summary: PPTX theme `<a:srgbClr val>` sink bypasses the new `toRgbHexColor` normalizer the diff establishes for every other color sink
finding.evidence: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:83-84` still does `const hex = escapeXmlAttr(toSrgbHex(theme.colors[role]))` → `<a:srgbClr val="${hex}"/>`, where `toSrgbHex` (theme.ts:64) is only `hex.replace(/^#/,'').toUpperCase()`. The diff's new invariant (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:52-60: "every attribute this function emits is either [0-9A-F]{6}, a closed ROLE_TO_SCHEME value, or a finite number") does not hold for this file because it never routes through `colorChildXml`. `themes[]` is stored verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot` and the new `assertValidSlidesBody` validates only that `themes` is an array (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:472-478), so an API caller can put `rgb(255,0,0)`, `''`, or `a"/><x y="` in `theme.colors[role]` and the exported deck carries a schema-invalid (escaped-but-non-hex) `ST_HexColorRGB` that PowerPoint refuses to open.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:83-84 emits `<a:srgbClr val="${escapeXmlAttr(toSrgbHex(theme.colors[role]))}"/>`, and toSrgbHex (theme.ts:64-66) only strips a leading '#' and uppercases — it does not validate to six hex digits and never routes through toRgbHexColor/colorChildXml. The invariant the diff establishes is real and stated repo-wide (color.ts:29-31 'every attribute this function emits is either [0-9A-F]{6}, a closed ROLE_TO_SCHEME value, or a finite number'; color.ts:59 `toRgbHexColor(c.value) ?? '000000'`), and the sibling sink text.ts:208 was updated while theme.ts was not; the design doc (slides-pptx-export.md:151-167) enumerates only the omittable (text.ts) and mandatory (colorChildXml) sinks, leaving the theme clrScheme sink uncovered. The path is reachable with untrusted data: assertValidSlidesBody checks only Array.isArray for 'themes' (docs-content.controller.ts:472-478) with no walk of themes[*].colors, the body is stored verbatim via writeSlidesRoot (controller.ts:193), and export feeds deck.themes[0] straight to themeToXml (export/pptx/index.ts:178-183), reachable from frontend pptx-actions.ts:92 and cli pptx-export.ts:18. No guard makes it unreachable: escapeXmlAttr (xml.ts:5-12) prevents raw injection but does not make 'rgb(255, 0, 0)' or '' a valid ST_HexColorRGB, and ColorScheme values are plain strings (model/theme.ts:1-26). This is exactly the blast-radius lane — a normalization contract applied at every other color sink with a bypassing sink in a file the diff does not show.

finding.evidence: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts:122/143 `DASH_VAL[stroke.dash] ?? 'dash'` → `<a:prstDash val="…"/>`; packages/slides/src/export/pptx/connector.ts:55-56 `KIND_TO_OOXML[a.kind] ?? 'triangle'` / `SIZE_TO_OOXML[a.size] ?? 'med'`; packages/slides/src/export/pptx/layout.ts:53 `BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE[layout.id] ?? 'blank'`. All four read persisted, PUT-settable values (`stroke.dash`, arrowhead kind/size, `layouts[].id` — none validated by the new `assertValidLayout`), so a stored `'constructor'`/`'toString'` resolves to an inherited `Object.prototype` member, survives the `??` fallback and is stringified into an OOXML attribute — the precise failure mode the diff documents at packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:62-69 and packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:110-118.

verdict.reason: All four claimed object-literal lookups exist verbatim: DASH_VAL (shape.ts:122) used at shape.ts:143 into an unescaped <a:prstDash val=...>; KIND_TO_OOXML/SIZE_TO_OOXML (connector.ts:30,47) used at connector.ts:55-56 into type/w/len attributes; BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE (layout.ts:24) used at layout.ts:53 into the <p:sldLayout type> attribute. The diff's own rationale for converting the sibling lookups to Maps is present at text.ts:61-69 and docx-style-map.ts:110-123 ("an object lookup walks the prototype chain ... survive the ?? fallback"), so the failure mode is acknowledged by the change itself. Reachability is not blocked upstream: the new PUT validators only walk text bodies (assertValidElementData:612-642 inspects data.text/data.rows/data.children only, never data.stroke or data.arrowheads) and assertValidLayout:499-516 never validates layout.id, so these values are persisted verbatim and reach the sinks. No not-present, already-guarded, or counterexample ground applies; the sinks are outside the diff's guarded lines, which is squarely this lens's lane.

finding.summary: The new slide-text block validation is reachable around: only slides[*].elements is walked, while layouts[*].staticElements, masters[*] elements and slides[*].notes carry the same docs Blocks through the same PUT into the same layout engine and exporters, unvalidated.
finding.evidence: assertValidSlidesBody only loops b.slides (docs-content.controller.ts:459-462) and assertValidSlide merely checks Array.isArray(s.notes) (line 490). But Slide.notes: Block[] (packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:45) and layout/master staticElements (packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:70,80,105) hold the same docs Block / element shapes the new assertValidTextBodyBlocks guards for slides[*].elements. writeSlidesRoot (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:93) bulk-assigns layouts, masters and notes verbatim, so the exact out-of-range style.alignment or non-finite marginTop the diff now rejects via slides[i].elements[j].data.blocks still reaches the deck via layouts[k].staticElements[j].data.blocks or slides[i].notes[n].style on the same endpoint.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the new slide-block validation only walks slides[*].elements, leaving layouts[*].staticElements, masters and slides[*].notes as unguarded paths carrying the same docs Blocks through the same PUT. All three claimed gaps are already closed in the same file. (1) assertValidSlidesBody does not end at line 462: docs-content.controller.ts:493-496 loops b.layouts through assertValidLayout, which at :507-515 walks BOTH 'placeholders' and 'staticElements' via assertValidNestedElement -> assertValidElementData (:612-641) -> assertValidTextBodyBlocks (:664-676) -> assertValidSlideBlocks -> assertValidBlockStyle (:698-702), the identical alignment/geometry guard applied to slides[*].elements. (2) assertValidSlide does not merely check Array.isArray(s.notes); after that array check at :543-547 it calls assertValidSlideBlocks(s.notes, path.notes) at :557, validating each note block's style (:692-703) and recursing into tableData cells (:704-718). (3) Master is { id, themeId, background, placeholderStyles } with PlaceholderStyle being scalar font/size/color/align/lineHeight fields (packages/slides/src/model/master.ts:4-10, 25-34); it carries no elements and no Blocks, so there is nothing of the guarded shape inside it. The reviewer's cited layout.ts:70,80,105 are 'staticElements: []' entries inside the BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS data literal, not block-bearing type declarations. No unvalidated path to the guarded Block shape through this endpoint was found.
